chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Roland Kirk and demanding discipline on the bandstand
summary: Kirk learned his compositions unprompted; Mingus insisted on finesse and ran the band hard.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah. Did -- you were talking about tailoring your music to the saxophone player who just passed away.
Roland Kirk, yeah. Most of the time, though, you expected the players to come in and adapt themselves to what you needed from them, to or get into the music.

Yeah. Well, see, I first heard Roland -- he came up and told me he'd like to play in my band. He said, 'I know your music.' I said, 'What do you mean, you know my music?' He said, 'I know some of your compositions.' And so he went and started playing them all by himself. So I hired him. Because he had that much respect to learn my music. When he had no reason to. He was living in another state when he learned that. He was from Chicago, wasn't he?
I don't know where he was from. I think it was Chicago.
The thing is, though, that you always, it seemed to me, insisted that the players respect your in + tensions
when you were playing. You used to always holler at them in the bandstand. Now, --
I wasn't hollering. I was singing out particularly points. parts.
No, I mean, I've heard you say things like, to Eric Dolphy, "Play with taste, man." And --
That's what I told Danny, he had no finesse. Earlier he did, but he didn't developed it. Now he has no finesse unless he gets back to his old self.

Because it seemed to me that some of the things that you made the players deal with on the bandstand were very, very difficult, and in order to surmount the complex kinds of structures that you had people play on, that they really had to -- that's probably why they learned so much, from having to deal with that.

But it certainly wasn't easy to play in a Charles Mingus band. You had to work your ass off to do it. I mean, you made sure of that, and there's no doubt whose band it was, either. No, I mean, it was -- you really ran the band. And --
